name: Barbell Incline Bench Press
equipmentItems: Rack with safety supports or a competent spotter
grip: Overhand pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder width with thumbs wrapped securely around the bar.
description: Press a barbell from the upper chest while lying on an incline bench angled between 30 and 45 degrees, developing upper pectoral thickness and anterior deltoid strength.
setup: Set an incline bench between 30 and 45 degrees inside a power rack or designated incline bench station.
Lie on the bench with eyes positioned directly under the racked barbell, feet flat and firmly pressed into the floor.
Retract and depress your scapulae, planting your shoulder blades firmly into the bench pad.
Grasp the bar with a full overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width, wrists straight.
Unrack the barbell and settle it directly over the upper chest with arms straight and elbows softly unlocked.
instructions: Lower the bar smoothly toward your upper chest (at or slightly below the clavicles), keeping elbows tucked at approximately a 45 to 60-degree angle to the torso.
Touch the barbell lightly to the chest without bouncing off the sternum.
Press the bar upward and slightly backward along an efficient diagonal pressing path until arms are fully extended over the shoulders.
Maintain leg drive and tight upper back tension throughout the entire repetition.
cues: Pull the bar down to the upper chest.
commonMistakes: Setting bench angle excessively steep (e.g. 60+ degrees), transforming the exercise into a shoulder press.
Bouncing the barbell violently off the chest.
Flaring elbows straight out to 90 degrees, stressing the anterior shoulder capsule.

logging.example: Standard 20 kg barbell loaded with two 20 kg plates (one per side): record 60 kg total barbell mass.
logging.note: Record the total system mass of the barbell plus all loaded plates.

variantNote: Free-weight incline pressing movement angled at 30 to 45 degrees, providing unrestricted barbell path and demanding significant shoulder stabilizer engagement.
